text:
alex: seeing a spike in 502/504s from GPU pools in us-west-2 starting ~08:12 UTC, surfacing as model pull failures and connection resets
ops-bot: ALERT: nat-egress-error-rate > 5% across gw-usw2a,gw-usw2b at 08:15 UTC
maya: digging into worker logs now — lots of "connect(): cannot assign requested address" and repeated TCP RST on outbound to external registries
sam: that typically smells like SNAT port exhaustion on the NAT gateway or conntrack exhaustion on the node
jordan: CloudWatch for the NAT gateways shows heavy connection churn but no direct port metric (AWS gives bytes, not port count) — spikes correspond to our nightly model pulls + autoscaler bursts
alex: exact log excerpt: ```
2026-03-18T08:13:21Z model-downloader ERR fetch model v2 failed: dial tcp 52.216.32.10:443: connect: connection reset by peer
2026-03-18T08:13:21Z kubelet WARN create pod: image pull error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to copy: failed to copy layer: EOF
```
maya: also seeing a lot of sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT on the node side: `ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l` shows ~48k
sam: that matches ephemeral port range exhaustion — default ip_local_port_range + TIME_WAIT leaving very few source ports for new outbound connections
jordan: two-pronged mitigation plan: immediate mitigations to stop customer impact, and medium-term fixes to avoid repeat
alex: what immediate changes can we roll that are low-risk?
maya: immediate mitigations we can push in parallel: 1) add additional NAT gateways (one per AZ) to increase available SNAT port pool; 2) create S3/Gateway and ECR/VPC endpoints so model artifact and image pulls bypass NAT; 3) reduce autoscaler burst size for 15m while we stabilize
sam: +1 on VPC endpoints — that will remove the biggest chunk of ephemeral port churn quickly because most of these pulls are from S3/ECR. Also create a temporary pull-proxy (small fleet) inside the VPC that caches commonly used images/models
jordan: created a ticket for provisioning 2 more NAT gateways in usw2b/usw2c and attaching route table entries, ETA ~12m if no quota issues
ops-bot: TASK created: infra#3245 provision natgw-usw2b/usw2c (requester: jordan)
maya: sysctl knobs we can apply on nodes (temporary) to help: ```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 61000'
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
these were tested on staging, lowers TIME_WAIT pressure and increases conntrack capacity. We'll roll via daemonset to GPU node pool if folks agree
alex: any risk to changing nf_conntrack_max? need to ensure memory on nodes can handle more entries
sam: we already have headroom on node memory; set it conservatively and watch `conntrack -S` metrics. Also ensure kube-proxy conntrack settings aren't capping at a lower value
jordan: on longer-term fixes: 1) move image/model pulls to regional caches and S3 replication + VPC endpoints; 2) build a model prewarm job to pull artifacts into local cache before autoscaler adds workers; 3) add observability: infer/egress->estimate SNAT port saturation by extrapolating connections per second and TIME_WAIT windows, surface a synthetic "port-utilization" metric
maya: FYI we temporarily disabled a misbehaving canary job that was repeatedly pulling 200+ small files and hammering the NAT gateway — reduced outbound flows by ~28%
alex: sounds good. Jordan, proceed with NAT gateway add + route table updates. Sam & Maya, can you draft the daemonset with the sysctl changes and a conntrack exporter for quick rollout?
jordan: natgw add in progress, AWS quotas are fine, provisioning should be done by 08:25 UTC
sam: drafting daemonset now. Will include a readiness check and rollback hook. Will also add a small iptables rule to log any SYN floods to remote log aggregator for a few minutes so we can correlate
maya: after NAT gateways come up and VPC endpoints are added, we should run a short load test to validate no more port saturation — I'll queue the smoke test for 08:40 UTC
ops-bot: UPDATE: natgw-usw2b created at 08:23 UTC, natgw-usw2c created at 08:24 UTC
jordan: route tables updated, traffic started shifting. Early numbers show a 40% drop in connection reset errors in next 2 min
alex: massive thanks team. follow-ups: - ticket infra#3246 to add ECR+S3 endpoints permanently - infra#3247 to implement model pull cache - observability task infra#3248 for synthetic port-util metric
maya: also adding playbook notes: avoid tcp_tw_recycle (deprecated) and be mindful of kernel/kernel-versions differences across node types — we'll document exact sysctl values we applied
sam: putting a note to ops runbook: if you see similar spikes, prioritize S3/ECR endpoints first, then scale NAT gateways, then node sysctl changes
jordan: closing loop: post-mortem will include timeline, root cause: ephemeral port exhaustion driven by concurrent model/image pulls during autoscaler bursts plus a noisy job, mitigations applied, and long-term roadmap above
alex: ok closing thread once smoke test results are green. current status: degraded -> recovering
maya: smoke test passed at 08:41 UTC, no new connection resets observed in the next 10m window
ops-bot: INCIDENT resolved: nat-egress-error-rate < 1% as of 08:51 UTC
